title: Uber Ride Matching
description: Explore how Uber's dispatch system matches riders with drivers in real time, covering geospatial indexing, ETA estimation, and surge pricing.

data.text: Uber's core technical challenge is matching riders with drivers in real time. This requires geospatial indexing, real-time location tracking, ETA estimation, and dynamic pricing. The system must respond within milliseconds while handling millions of concurrent location updates.

The dispatch system must track millions of driver locations, process millions of ride requests per day, and match riders to drivers within 2-3 seconds. It must also handle driver acceptance/rejection, ETA updates, and dynamic pricing adjustments.

data.title: Ride Request Flow
items: Rider requests ride with pickup and destination
System geohashes rider location and queries nearby drivers
Top N drivers are ranked by ETA and proximity
Ride request is sent to top driver via push notification
Driver accepts or declines within 15 seconds
If declined, request moves to next driver
Matched driver's ETA is streamed to rider

data.title: Geospatial Indexing
data.text: Uber uses H3, a hexagonal hierarchical geospatial indexing system. Hexagons provide consistent neighbor relationships and minimize distortion at different zoom levels. Each driver is indexed by their current H3 cell.

Driver apps send GPS coordinates every 4-8 seconds. A Kafka pipeline ingests these updates, enriches them with H3 geohash, and writes to a Redis cluster for low-latency queries. The write path handles 10+ million updates per second during peak hours.

data.title: Uber Dispatch Lessons
points: Real-time matching requires sub-second geospatial queries
H3 hexagonal indexing outperforms square grids for proximity
Location pipelines need massive write throughput
Driver matching is a ranking problem, not just nearest-neighbor
Surge pricing is a supply-demand signal that influences matching
data.takeaway: Location-based systems require specialized indexing and real-time data pipelines that traditional databases cannot provide.

data.title: Design a Simple Dispatch
data.description: Design a dispatch system for a food delivery app with 100,000 drivers. Each driver reports location every 5 seconds. Riders request delivery within 30 minutes. Choose a geospatial index and justify your choice.
data.expectedOutcome: H3 at resolution 7-8 provides ~100m cells, enabling fast nearest-driver queries. Redis with H3 indexing handles 100K drivers at ~20K updates/sec.

items.question: How does Uber handle drivers with poor GPS signals?
items.answer: Uber uses Kalman filtering to smooth GPS noise and dead reckoning when GPS is unavailable. The system also weights recent GPS fixes more heavily.

items.question: Why not use a relational database for driver locations?
items.answer: Relational databases cannot handle 10M+ writes per second with sub-100ms geospatial queries. Specialized in-memory stores are required.
